Q: Do I need the `languageOptions.globals` field in eslint flat config when using typescript-eslint? A:

If you're linting TypeScript files with type information, you don't need to set globals, because TypeScript will properly deduce globals from type description files.

But if you're linting plain JavaScript files, then you often need globals.

Compare:

// save as test.{ts,js}
console.log('ok');

And lint:

npx eslint test.*

eslint will complain about console on test.js, but not on test.ts (because TypeScript will have handled this). You need globals: globals.node or globals: globals.browser for this to work.

Q: plt.savefig() truncates the image A:

As you suggested you can use subplot2grid for this. (Example in doc)

I use the same names as @NullDev because rest is the same.

# (1 row, 3 columns), (row,col), ...
ax_plot  = plt.subplot2grid((1, 3), (0, 0), colspan=2)
ax_table = plt.subplot2grid((1, 3), (0, 2))

Full code:

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Creating dataset
df = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "Month": ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun", "Jul", "Aug", "Sept", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec"],
        "2024": [1945, 1290, 1662, 1500, 1355, 1469, 1209, 1429, 1662, 1350, 1525, 1625],
        "2025": [1695, 1767, 1475, 1518, 1556, 1441, 1467, 1557, 1421, 1460, 950, 715],
    }
)

# (1 row, 3 columns), pos
ax_plot = plt.subplot2grid((1, 3), (0, 0), colspan=2)
ax_table = plt.subplot2grid((1, 3), (0, 2))

ax_plot.plot(df["Month"], df["2024"], "g", label="2024")
ax_plot.plot(df["Month"], df["2025"], "r", label="2025")
ax_plot.set_title("Revenues")

ax_table.axis("off")
ax_table.table(
    cellText=df.to_numpy(),
    colLabels=df.columns,
    loc="center",
    bbox=[0, 0, 1, 1],
)

plt.savefig("table_test.png")
plt.show()

Q: Spring Boot 3 + Testcontainers: Integration tests are being ignored without explicit error A:

In logs you can see: Can't get Docker image: RemoteDockerImage(imageName=mysql:8.4 ... Which means it can't fetch proper docker image and it is happening because docker image name or version is not correct.

You can change your code to something like following and make sure image name and version are provided:

new MySQLContainer<>("mysql:latest")

or use

docker image ls

to see list of images you have in docker and verify your required image is downloaded or not.

Q: Why x86 haven't instructions such instructions? A:

Also note this variant:

    mov   sp, @F
    jmp   func
@@: dw    @F   ; fake "stack" for return address
@@:
    ; execution continues here

func:
    ; do stuff, but be sure SP is restored/untouched
    ret

This allows standard stack-oriented leaf functions to be used in a RAM-less context as well.

Q: How to share Github Pages via link-only option? A:

In general, I don't know if there's a third-party tool to do the work, but it's easy to make it by hand, provides that you're not creating a lot of such pages.

First, is it possible to make a public GitHub Pages based on private repository?

Yes. Just create a private repository, head to Settings >> Options, find the section called "GitHub Pages" and set the source branch. This process is just the same as creating any GitHub pages.

P.S. you SHOULD see the message

Caution: This repository is private but the published site will be public.

This states exactly what you want.

only those with the URL can access the github.io website

Well, just make the URL difficult to guess.

For example, named the repository as a random string "uk5KKR". However, this will likely mess up the repositories in your profile, soon after you'll be difficult to find the correct repository that you need now. Instead, you can named name in this way: "githubpage_uk5KKR".

For other people, it's difficult to find this page when they are not provided the URL. And for you, just search "githubpage" in your profile and this repository should appear.

Here's a few notes:

  • You should adjust the length of the random string according to how secure you need.
  • It's also possible to make a quarantine area by the path name in a repository. For example, create paths "n2jnHG" and "4xSN2g" in the same repository of GitHub page, then the contents in these two paths could be shared with different people.
  • Finally, note that if anyone failed to keep the URL secret, the whole page is not secret anymore. It could even become an entry in Google search result.
